title: Telecom and fibre, 1990s
subtitle: Capacity builders, equipment and applications
description: Most inputs are judgement. The model has no supply-and-demand link, so a capacity glut shows up only through share drift. Read the What must be true panel and compare with What happened before reading anything into the verdicts.
asOfRule: Last quarter-end before the primary equity index peak (Nasdaq Composite, 10 March 2000; to be verified). Uses hindsight; applied the same way as for the railway case.
hindsightDisclosure: Scored by someone who knew the outcome: that telecom capacity was overbuilt, that carriers and suppliers lost most of their value in 2000-2002, and that Internet traffic nonetheless kept roughly doubling each year.

pool.note: Sum of the three layers' full-adoption revenue: 11.1 + 50.0 + 60.0.

speed.note: Traffic about doubling each year; speed = ln(81)/ln(2) x doubling time of 1 year = 6.34, rounded to 6.3.

mid.note: Reference midpoint, rounded: speed / 2 = 3.15, stored as 3.2. The reference curve therefore starts at about, not exactly, 10% of full adoption. Offsets are computed from the stored values.

disc.note: No period source pulled; high sensitivity.

evidence.note: Traffic growth about 100% a year; no measured paid revenue per unit of capacity.

share.note: Full-adoption revenue $11.1bn (judgement; P2): 10% of the $110.9bn 1997 US long-distance ($104.6bn) plus Internet services ($6.3bn) market. The 10% is my choice. Arithmetic: 11.1 / 121.1. Both figures are judgement.

offset.note: Derived (numerator sourced, denominator judgement). Year-0 adoption f = Level 3's 1998 revenue $0.392bn (P2, sourced) / full-adoption revenue $11.1bn (judgement) = 0.0353. offset = ln((1 - f) / f) / k - midpoint, using the stored speed 6.3 and midpoint 3.2: k = ln(81) / 6.3 = 0.6975; ln((1 - f) / f) = 3.3075; 3.3075 / 0.6975 - 3.2 = 1.5417, kept to two decimals: 1.54. Level 3's total 1998 revenue of $392m includes non-telecom businesses, so f is probably overstated.

capex.note: $2.3bn expected 1999 capex x 3 years, assuming the 1999 pace holds.

buildYears.note: The filing plans network completion by Q1 2001.

speed.note: The reported 10-fold yearly growth in bandwidth gives a doubling time of ln 2 / ln 10 = 0.30 years; speed = 6.34 x 0.30 = 1.9. Year-0 adoption is sensitive to rounding at this speed; offsets are computed from the stored speed and midpoint and kept to two decimals.

mid.note: Reference midpoint, rounded: speed / 2 = 0.95, stored as 1.0. The reference curve therefore starts at about, not exactly, 10% of full adoption. Offsets are computed from the stored values.

offset.note: Derived (numerator sourced, denominator judgement). Year-0 adoption f = Level 3's 1998 revenue $0.392bn (P2, sourced) / full-adoption revenue $11.1bn (judgement) = 0.0353. offset = ln((1 - f) / f) / k - midpoint, using the stored speed 1.9 and midpoint 1.0: k = ln(81) / 1.9 = 2.3129; ln((1 - f) / f) = 3.3075; 3.3075 / 2.3129 - 1.0 = 0.4300, kept to two decimals: 0.43. Level 3's total 1998 revenue of $392m includes non-telecom businesses, so f is probably overstated.

outcomes.summary: Capex ran above plan and outlay far exceeded revenue.
Revenue fell from $38.3bn in FY1999 (period filing P3, listed under sources) to $12.3bn in FY2002 and $9.0bn in FY2004; the scopes differ (restated basis).
For: Yahoo, Amazon and eBay were still in the basket in 2003. Against: only 13 of the original 20 remained and long-run excess returns for Internet stocks after lockup expiry were as low as -33%.
